prompt: Finish the Savings subclass of the provided abstract Account, add addInterest(rate), and write a static totalFees(Account[]) that proves dynamic dispatch. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Account is abstract: it supplies shared state and behaviour but leaves monthlyFee() for each subclass to answer. Its balance is private, so even Savings must go through deposit/getBalance/setBalance -- encapsulation holds inside the hierarchy too. totalFees loops over an Account[] and calls monthlyFee() on each element; the compiler only knows the static type Account, but at runtime the JVM dispatches to the actual object's override, so Savings answers 0.0 and Checking answers 12.0 from the very same line of code. That is polymorphism doing the branching for you instead of a chain of if statements.
hints: addInterest must not touch balance directly -- it is private to Account. Read it with getBalance() and store the new value with setBalance(...).
Interest on 200.0 at rate 0.10 is 200.0 * 0.10 = 20.0, giving 220.0. So the new balance is getBalance() + getBalance() * rate.
In totalFees use an enhanced for loop over the array and add account.monthlyFee() each time -- no instanceof or casting needed.
